title: thread — one prospective entry, open or watch
description:
A forward-intent entry in a shed record: an open thread (polarity `open`, lives in `open_threads`: something to pick up, with a next step) or a watch-out (polarity `watch`, lives in `watch_outs`: something to keep true, or to avoid). Prospective, so it carries a LEASE (lease.json rides flat here); the discharge test rides as `done_when` on an open thread and `still_true` on a watch-out — the shipping evaluators' names.

Every entry names who stands behind it (`tier`, required). `authored` needs nothing further. `derived` and `interpreted` must carry `evidence` — a verbatim quote and the transcript turn it came from — and finalize rejects the entry unless the quote is a substring of that turn: a proof-block gate applied to prose. A bare string is unknown-author and is rejected.

Carry forward by copying, never by restating: an entry carried from an earlier archive names `origin_sid8` and must be byte-identical to an entry in that archive (`content_sha256`, S1, makes the check a hash). Identity is origin plus succession (S2): `id` = `<origin_sid8>/<ordinal>` assigned once, and `supersedes` points at the entry this one replaces, with the reason — one semantic shared with intent.superseded, the brief lifecycle and LBP-Wire §10, in one costume.

A brief is not a noun here: it is a thread that escaped into its own file to be suggested to a stranger. At level zero, threads suffice.

polarity.description: Which kind of thread. Implied by the record field the entry sits in (`open_threads` → open, `watch_outs` → watch); stated only when the entry travels alone (a room event, a fixture).

thread.description: Open polarity: the unresolved item, named.

next_step.description: Open polarity: the concrete next action.

blockers.description: Open polarity: what is in the way, if anything. A non-empty value does NOT imply a failed status.

status.description: Open polarity, optional: marks a genuinely FAILED thread. Absence = a normal open thread.

text.description: Watch polarity: the warning, in one or two sentences.

gloss.description: Free prose about the entry — the paraphrase, the why, the model's reading. NEVER gated, always rendered as the entry's tier. The claim lives in `thread` / `text` and must be a verbatim span of the cited turn; anything the writer wants to add in its own words goes here, where a reader can see it is not a quotation.

evidence.description: Required on derived / interpreted entries. `turn` is a transcript turn index or uuid; the entry's CLAIM TEXT (`thread` on an open thread, `text` on a watch-out) must be a verbatim substring of that turn's text, or finalize rejects it. `quote` is optional and, when present, must be a substring too; it is no longer what the gate is about — an attached quote bound nothing (a fabricated thread beside a real, unrelated quote passed the earlier gate). Basis at entry granularity: the instrument is the transcript, the substring test is the reproduction.

intent_verdict.description: Set when the entry was written by finalize from the session's declared intent (`declare`): the statement, verbatim and authored, carrying its own done_when. MET never becomes a thread — it becomes a progress line.

origin_sid8.description: Set when the entry is carried from an earlier archive: the sid8 of that archive. The entry must then be byte-identical (minus this key and content_sha256) to an entry in it.

content_sha256.description: S1: sha256 of the source entry's canonical JSON (sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, minus `origin_sid8` and `content_sha256`). Beside `origin_sid8` this makes the carry check a hash rather than a byte-compare, and is the `tension_target` a later disposition binds to.

id.description: S2: `<origin_sid8>/<ordinal>` — assigned when the entry is first written, kept verbatim when carried. Identity = origin; succession is `supersedes`.

supersedes.description: S2: the entry this one replaces, and why. A restated thread is a NEW entry that supersedes the old one — never an edit of the carried copy.
